rationale: Hu et al. (2024) systematically reviewed reported SCAF4 variants alongside three novel cases, reporting that variants in domain-encoding and upstream exons demonstrated a strong association with epileptic seizures. However, subsequent case reports and larger cohort expansions directly complicate this assertion: Chen et al. (2025) identified a patient harboring an RRM domain variant (c.1693C>T, p.Arg565*) who exhibited no seizures, while the expanded cohort of 50 individuals analyzed by Schmid et al. (2025) highlights incomplete and variable penetrance of seizures across a broader molecular spectrum without validating a strict domain-delimited risk dichotomy.

evidence.text: Systematic review of SCAF4 variants indicated that variants located in domain-encoding exons and upstream exons showed a strong association with epilepsy.

source.title: SCAF4 variants are associated with epilepsy with neurodevelopmental disorders
source.quote: The variants in the domain-encoding exons and upstream exons exhibited a strong association with epilepsy.

evidence.text: A patient harboring a nonsense mutation (c.1693C>T, p.Arg565*) located within the functional RRM region of SCAF4 presented with neurodevelopmental symptoms without any observed epileptic seizures.

evidence.text: Characterization of an expanded cohort of 50 individuals demonstrated variable clinical penetrance of seizures and neurodevelopmental features across diverse truncating, missense, and splice-site variants.

source.title: Further delineation of the SCAF4-associated neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: We assembled data on 50 novel individuals with SCAF4 variants ascertained via GeneMatcher and personal communication... Frequent clinical findings were mild developmental delay with speech impairment, seizures, and skeletal abnormalities

evidence.text: Analysis of nine individuals with likely gene-disrupting variants residing across the N-terminal two-thirds of SCAF4 demonstrated seizures alongside mild intellectual disability and skeletal anomalies.

source.title: Variants in SCAF4 cause a neurodevelopmental disorder and are associated with impaired mRNA processing
source.journal: The American Journal of Human Genetics
source.quote: Using exome sequencing and international matchmaking, we identified nine likely pathogenic germline variants in SCAF4 including two splice-site and seven truncating variants, all residing in the N-terminal two thirds of the protein.

conflicts: Hu et al. (2024) proposed that domain-encoding and upstream variants strongly associate with seizures, whereas Chen et al. (2025) reported an individual carrying a variant in the RRM domain who manifested no seizures.

Cohort data from Schmid et al. (2025) demonstrate broad and incomplete penetrance of epilepsy across disparate variant types and locations throughout SCAF4 rather than a clearly segregated spatial risk boundary.

new_directions.question_text: Does statistical survival analysis of seizure-free intervals across the 50-individual Schmid et al. cohort confirm a higher cumulative incidence of seizures in domain/upstream variants versus downstream variants?
new_directions.rationale: Initial cohorts suffered from ascertainment bias towards epilepsy panels (e.g., Hu et al.), requiring unbiased analysis of age-at-onset curves across comprehensive multicenter cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: Do truncating variants upstream of the RRM domain induce complete nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) versus downstream truncating variants producing dominant-negative truncated SCAF4 isoforms?
new_directions.rationale: Determining whether the phenotypic variation is driven by functional domain disruption or varying degrees of NMD escape will clarify the mechanistic plausibility of position-dependent seizure penetrance.
